memory: Tensor project (2026-10-03): Tensor is Milvow's internal GTM system: find B2B prospects, research them with evidence, pick an offer, write personalised cold email, track replies, learn. Detail lives in docs/TENSOR-FOUNDATION.md and docs/HERMES-INTEGRATION.md in milvow-ai/Tensor.
Tensor (2026-10-03): the user wants work done in phases: collect resources first, then design, then develop. Do not build before the design is approved.
Tensor (2026-10-03): the user is very sensitive to token spend. Prefer lean execution, use no research subagents unless asked, and stop workers when told.

Tensor (2026-10-03): the user wants to be asked when something is unclear rather than having Claude assume. They use the orchestrate skill (lead plans, workers build, checks gate, lead commits), saved in the repo under .claude/.
Tensor constraints (2026-10-03): budget is about $0 until the first client. It runs on the founder's own PC (likely Windows) with no VPS; the old n8n VPS has expired.
Tensor market (2026-10-03): initial targets are US and Canada small-to-mid B2B companies. The offers are A (website experience) and B (AI workflow automation); verticals are deliberately not assumed.
Milvow (2026-10-02): milvow.com mail runs on Zoho (India DC) with SPF include:zoho.in, DKIM selector zmail and DMARC p=none. The domain is at Namecheap with auto-renew OFF, expiring 2027-08-17.

Milvow (2026-10-02): the Cigna and Aetna case-study links on milvow.com redirect to the homepage, and /pricing redirects to /contact. Prospects will check the site, so the user must confirm the case studies are real or remove them.

Milvow accounts (2026-10-02): the Supabase org has 3 paused projects (the free plan allows 2 active). A Clay workspace is connected through MCP with 19 enrichment functions; Firecrawl credits ran out on 2026-10-03.

Tensor (2026-10-03): GitHub pushes to milvow-ai/Tensor fail with 403 until the Claude GitHub App is installed on the repo. Commits on branch claude/awesome-archimedes-vb1t7y existed only in the cloud container.

Tensor email finding (2026-10-03): no ToS-clean $0 cold-email sending path exists. Zoho Free has no SMTP/IMAP and Zoho policy demands express permission; SES, Resend, Postmark, Brevo, Mailgun and SendGrid ban cold lists.

Tensor email decision (2026-10-03): the recommended start is one Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 mailbox (about $7–8/month) on a separate outreach domain. Never send cold mail from milvow.com's Zoho, because a suspension would hit the agency's real email.

Tensor compliance (2026-10-03): Canadian law (CASL) allows cold B2B email only with implied consent under s.10(9)(b): address conspicuously published, no no-spam notice, message relevant to the role. The sender carries the proof (s.13); penalties reach C$10M, so Tensor must store publication evidence per Canadian contact.

Tensor compliance (2026-10-03): US cold email follows CAN-SPAM (opt-out, honest headers, postal address, unsubscribe). Every email needs a footer with the business name, postal address and opt-out line.

Tensor deliverability (2026-10-03): Gmail wants spam rate under 0.10% and never 0.30%; Postmaster Tools hides low-volume data, so Tensor must count bounces and complaints itself. Plan for 10–30 sends per mailbox per day with a ramp.
Tensor benchmarks (2026-10-03): cold-email reply-rate benchmarks conflict (Instantly 3.43% vs Belkins 0.45%), and every producer sells in the space (Low grade). Plan with pessimistic numbers.

Tensor providers (2026-10-03): Apollo's API works on all plans including Free. People search costs 0 credits, org search 1 credit/page, enrichment 1 credit (charged when found); Free gives 900 credits/yr.
Tensor providers (2026-10-03): Apollo's ToS bars multiple self-serve accounts and circumventing limits, so use one connection only. The user agreed they cannot connect two accounts of any tool.

Tensor providers (2026-10-03): Clay's HTTP API and webhooks need the Growth plan ($495/mo). At $0, Clay is usable only through MCP, either by hand or by a supervised agent; Free gives 100 data credits + 500 actions/mo.
Tensor providers (2026-10-03): the Meta Ad Library API does not return US/Canada commercial ads, and scraping its UI needs Meta's written permission. Ads checks are a human evidence task.
Tensor providers (2026-10-03): free verification is Reoon (20/day + 100 at signup) and ZeroBounce (100/mo); MillionVerifier ($89/50k) is the paid overflow. Treat catch-all addresses as risky.

Tensor web evidence (2026-10-03): cite only screenshot-confirmed website facts and dated CrUX p75 values. Never cite Lighthouse scores, axe counts or revenue-loss claims; PSI v5 is free (~25k/day, secondary source).

Tensor AI layer (2026-10-03): GitHub Models was retired 2026-07-30, Cerebras has no free tier, and the Gemini free tier is small and trains on data. Groq Free (1K req/day per model), OpenRouter :free, Cloudflare Workers AI and local Ollama are the free options.

Tensor AI layer (2026-10-03): the Claude subscription may be used only via the unmodified claude CLI in own scripts (`-p --output-format json --json-schema`), never inside LiteLLM or SDK code. Docs say --bare (API key) becomes the -p default, so plan an API-key worker.

Tensor AI layer (2026-10-03): LiteLLM PyPI 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were malicious on 2026-03-24, so a thin router over OpenAI-compatible endpoints is preferred. Claude prices: Sonnet 5.5 $2/$10, Opus 5.5 $4/$20, Haiku 4.5 $1/$5 per MTok; Batch is -50%.

Tensor market data (2026-10-03): Census BTOS shows US AI use at 19.8% overall, with professional-technical 34% and construction 9%; StatCan shows similar. Larger firms (20+ staff) use outside help more; the default ICP is 20–249 staff.

Tensor market (2026-10-03): candidate pilot verticals are accounting 5412 (B), insurance agencies 5242 (B), consulting 5416 or engineering 5413 (A), and one low-maturity vertical (4238 or 332, both offers). These are judgements to test with equal-size pilots; BLS OEWS, SUSB and StatCan counts were not retrieved.

Tensor architecture (2026-10-03): a modular monolith with hexagonal provider adapters (anti-corruption layer) and a canonical, provider-neutral schema. Postgres 18 is the system of record and DBOS Transact handles workflows, queues, rate limits and dedup.

Tensor architecture (2026-10-03): the knowledge layer stores field-level facts with provenance, observed/verified/expires timestamps and evidence ids. Lookup is fresh → use, stale → policy, missing → acquire; identical requests are single-flighted by request hash.

Tensor architecture (2026-10-03): the Resource Manager ('Harness Farm') holds a provider registry, a consumption model per connection (any unit), an atomic quota ledger, free-first routing, health and circuit breakers. Executor types are api, local, llm, agent (Hermes or Claude CLI) and human.

Tensor architecture (2026-10-03): observations (seen, with evidence) are stored separately from inferred opportunities. Every email claim must cite an evidence id; a code check and a different-family verifier model check claims before human approval.

Tensor dashboard (2026-10-03): build a thin SPA (shadcn/ui starter, React Flow pipeline editor, RJSF forms generated from Pydantic schemas, TanStack Table, Recharts) instead of adopting n8n or Windmill. The overview mockup was generated with GPT from Claude's spec.

Hermes facts (2026-10-03): Hermes Agent (NousResearch, MIT) was studied at commit c8301ea6. It has an AIAgent Python API, a one-shot CLI with --usage-file (tokens + estimated cost), an OpenAI-compatible API server on port 8642, an MCP client (stdio/HTTP, OAuth) and middleware that can wrap or replace any tool call.

Hermes limits (2026-10-03): Hermes keeps screenshots only 24h, saves no HTML or hashes, and ignores robots.txt. Its defaults are risky: unlimited iterations, unsandboxed local terminal, keyless web fallbacks that send queries to vendors, email delivery paths, and no schema-enforced final answer.

Tensor + Hermes (2026-10-03): Hermes is the agent executor for exploratory work (website flows, published-email discovery for CASL, deep research, market research) plus dev and ops roles. It acts only through policy-gated Tensor MCP tools, submits structured results via submit tools, and has its tokens metered by a Tensor model gateway.

Tensor + Hermes (2026-10-03): Hermes never sends email, never holds provider keys or DB credentials, and never decides compliance, quotas or scoring. Evidence is captured by Tensor's own Playwright service, and Hermes sits behind an AgentExecutor port with the Claude CLI as the alternative.

Tensor strategy (2026-10-03): Claude advised that building the full Tensor before any outreach is the wrong order. Start AI-assisted outreach immediately, fix the website credibility issues, and build in thin slices driven by real pain.

Tensor current plan (2026-10-03): the user chose to build only Harness v0 first: registry, quota ledger, router, fact cache, evidence capture, suppression and CASL records, exposed as one MCP server. Claude and Hermes then run daily operations through it while the user approves and sends; the dashboard and pipeline come later if it works.

Tensor estimates (2026-10-03): Harness v0 is about 3–4k LOC, 2–3 days and 3–5M tokens. The MVP slice is about 4 days; full Tensor is about 16 working days (range 11–24) and 20–40M tokens, using Claude as lead with Gemini/Qwen as builders.
Tensor runtime (2026-10-03): operations must run on the user's PC (Claude Code + Hermes + harness MCP). The Claude cloud container's network reaches only GitHub, PyPI and npm.

Tensor open questions (2026-10-03): still needed are the Claude plan (Pro or Max), the database choice (Supabase free recommended vs local Postgres), free API keys in the PC .env, sender identity plus legal name and postal address, the outreach mailbox approval, and GitHub App install.
